source_text:
ἔργων προφητείαν ἀλληγορίαν ὠνόμασεν. Gal 4,25 Οὐχ ἁπλῶς ἐμνημόνευσε τοῦ
Σινᾶ ὄρους, ἀλλ' ἐπειδὴ οἱ Ἀγαρηνοὶ οἱ ἀπὸ τοῦ Ἰσμαὴλ τὴν ἔρημον ἔχουσι τὴν
παρατείνουσαν ἕως τοῦ Σινᾶ ὄρους. ἐν δὲ τῷ Σινᾷ ὁ νόμος ἐδόθη εἰς δουλείαν
γεννῶν, ἀπὸ δὲ τοῦ Σινᾶ ὄρους αἱ πλάκες δοθεῖσαι ἐκομίσθησαν ἐν τῷ Ἰσραήλ, καὶ
πολλάκις μετενεχθεῖσαι ἀπὸ τόπου εἰς τόπον τελευταῖον ἱδρύθησαν ἐν
Ἱεροσολύμοις. διὰ τοῦτο ἐπήγαγεν· συστοιχεῖ δὲ τῇ νῦν Ἱερουσαλήμ, δουλεύει δὲ
μετὰ τῶν τέκνων αὐτῆς. ὅπου γῆς ἐπαγγελία, καὶ κτῆσις καὶ γάμος καὶ τὰ
ἀνθρώπινα, καὶ δουλεία ἀκολουθεῖ· ὅπου δὲ ἀπαλλαγὴ τῶν ἐπὶ γῆς φροντίδων καὶ
τῶν δεσμῶν, καὶ ἐν οὐρανοῖς ἡ πολιτεία, ἐξ αὐτῆς τῆς πολιτείας ἡ ἐλευθερία. Gal
5,17 Ζητεῖται διὰ τί νόμου ἀποσπῶν μέμνηται τῆς ἁμαρτίας. ἐπειδὴ τρυφᾶν ἐκέλευεν
ὁ νόμος, διὰ δὲ τούτου διερεθίζεται ἡ ἐπιθυμία καὶ ἀκατάσχετος οὖσα πρὸς ἁμαρτίαν
ἄγει. τούτου ἕνεκεν ὅτε νόμου ἦν μνήμη, μέμνηται καὶ τῆς ἁμαρτίας. καὶ γὰρ ἐν τῇ
πρὸς Ῥωμαίους τοῦ νόμου μνημονεύων καὶ τῆς διὰ τοῦ κυρίου διορθώσεως
εἰσήγαγεν, τὸ οἱ γὰρ κατὰ σάρκα ζῶντες θεῷ ἀρέσαι οὐ δύνανται. διὰ τί δὲ
συνεχωρήθη τὸ τρυφᾶν καὶ ἐσθίειν; ὅτι ἡ τῶν ὡμολογημένων κακῶν ἀποχὴ οὐκ ἂν
προεχώρησεν, εἰ μὴ ἐνεδόθη αὐτοῖς τὸ ἐσθίειν 304 καὶ πίνειν· ᾔδει μὲν γὰρ ὁ
νομοθέτης ὅτι ἀδύνατον τρυφῶντας κρατεῖν ἡδονῶν. τέως δὲ ἠθέλησε τὸν νοῦν
παιδεῦσαι, ἵνα γνῷ τί καλὸν καὶ τί κακὸν καὶ τί τὸ εὐσεβές· προεώρα γὰρ ὅτι ἔμελλεν
ἔρχεσθαι ὁ τὸ λεῖπον τῷ νόμῳ προστιθείς, λέγω δὴ τὸ μὴ κατὰ σάρκα περιπατεῖν, ὡς
λέγει ὁ Παῦλος. Gal 6,7–8 Ἐδήλωσεν ἐκ τούτου ὅτι πολλοὶ ἀκαίρως μὲν ἀνήλισκον,
παρέχοντες τοῖς τηρεῖν νόμον παρακελευομένοις, τοῖς δὲ τὴν Παύλου διδασκαλίαν
κηρύττουσιν οὐδὲν παρεῖχον. διό φησιν· ὁ σπείρων εἰς τὴν σάρκα αὐτοῦ· ὁ γὰρ νόμῳ
ὑποκείμενος ἐν τοῖς σαρκικοῖς ζῇ. ὁ τοίνυν τῷ ταῦτα διδάσκοντι παρέχων εἰς τὴν
σάρκα σπείρει μόνον. Gal 6,14–15 Ἵνα μὴ νομισθῇ ἀκροβυστίας ἀντιποιεῖσθαι, καὶ
οὐχὶ περιτομῆς καὶ διαβολῆς πρόφασιν δῷ τοῖς ἀντιλέγουσιν, κάλλιστα ἐπήγαγε τὸ
τελευταῖον, ὅτι οὔτε περιτομή τι ἰσχύει οὔτε ἀκροβυστία, καινὴν δὲ κτίσιν εἶπεν.
περὶ ἧς ἀλλαχοῦ· εἴ τις ἐν Χριστῷ, καινὴ κτίσις. εἰ καινή, φησί, κτίσις, μὴ γίνου ὑπὸ
νόμον· ὁ γὰρ ζῶν κατὰ νόμον ἐν κόσμῳ ζῇ, ὁ δὲ ζῶν ἐν Χριστῷ, ἐν οὐρανοῖς
πολιτεύεται. ἐσταύρωται οὖν ἐμοὶ κόσμος κἀγὼ κόσμῳ.
pass_a_gloss:
[continuing from the previous section] ... deeds he named allegory.
Galatians 4:25. Not simply (idly) did he mention Mount Sinai, but because the Hagarenes, those from Ishmael, hold the desert that stretches as far as Mount Sinai. And on Sinai the law was given, bearing children into slavery, and from Mount Sinai the tablets that had been given were carried in Israel, and having often been moved from place to place, at last they were set up in Jerusalem. For this reason he added: "and it corresponds to the present Jerusalem, and it is in slavery with its children." Where there is promise of land, and possession and marriage and human things, slavery also follows; but where there is release from the cares on earth and from the bonds, and the citizenship is in the heavens, from that very citizenship comes freedom.
Galatians 5:17. It is asked why, while drawing (them) away from the law, he makes mention of sin. Because the law bade them live in plenty (enjoy themselves), and through this desire is stirred up and, being unrestrainable, leads toward sin. For this reason, when there was mention of the law, he mentions sin too. For also in the letter to the Romans, mentioning the law, he brought in also the correction through the Lord: "for those who live according to the flesh cannot please God." And why was living in plenty and eating allowed? Because the abstaining from evils that are acknowledged would not have advanced, unless eating and drinking had been granted to them. For the lawgiver knew that it is impossible for those living in plenty to master pleasures. But for the time being he wanted to train the mind, so that it might know what is good and what is bad and what is the pious thing; for he foresaw that there was to come the one who adds what is lacking to the law, I mean, not walking according to the flesh, as Paul says.
Galatians 6:7-8. He made plain from this that many were spending out of season, supplying those who were urging them to keep the law, but to those who preached the teaching of Paul they supplied nothing. Therefore he says: "the one who sows to his own flesh"; for the one subject to law lives in fleshly things. So the one who supplies the one who teaches these things sows only to the flesh.
Galatians 6:14-15. So that he might not be thought to lay claim to uncircumcision and not to circumcision, and give a pretext for slander to those who speak against him, he most finely added the last thing: that neither circumcision is anything strong nor uncircumcision, but he spoke of a new creation. Concerning which (he says) elsewhere: "if anyone is in Christ, a new creation." If a new creation, he says, do not come under law; for the one who lives according to law lives in the world, but the one who lives in Christ has citizenship in the heavens. So "the world has been crucified to me and I to the world."
pass_b_english: On Galatians 4:25: He did not mention Mount Sinai idly. He did it because the Hagarenes, the descendants of Ishmael, hold the desert that runs right up to Mount Sinai. It was on Sinai that the law was given, the law that bears children for slavery. The tablets given on Mount Sinai were carried about in Israel, moved again and again from place to place, and at last set up in Jerusalem. That is why he added: “It corresponds to the present Jerusalem, for she is in slavery with her children.” Wherever there is a promise of land, with property and marriage and all the business of human life, slavery follows. But where there is release from earthly cares and ties, and our citizenship is in heaven, freedom comes from that citizenship itself.

On Galatians 5:17: People ask why, while he is drawing them away from the law, he speaks about sin. The reason is that the law told them to enjoy plenty. That stirs up desire, and desire, once it cannot be held back, leads on to sin. So whenever he mentioned the law, he mentioned sin as well. In the letter to the Romans too, when he speaks of the law, he also brings in the correction that came through the Lord: “For those who live according to the flesh cannot please God” (Romans 8:8). Why, then, were feasting and eating allowed at all? Because they would not have made progress in keeping away from evils everyone admits to be evils, unless they had been allowed to eat and drink. The lawgiver knew, of course, that people who live in plenty cannot master their pleasures. For the time being, though, he wanted to train the mind, so that it would know what is good, what is evil and what is godly. He foresaw that someone was coming who would add what the law lacked: I mean not walking according to the flesh, as Paul puts it (Romans 8:4).

On Galatians 6:7–8: Here he makes it plain that many were spending their money unwisely. They supplied the men who were urging them to keep the law and gave nothing to those who preached Paul’s teaching. That is why he says, “He who sows to his own flesh”; for anyone subject to the law lives among the things of the flesh. So whoever supports a man who teaches such things is sowing to the flesh and nothing more.

On Galatians 6:14–15: He did not want to be thought to be championing uncircumcision against circumcision, and so hand his opponents an excuse to slander him. So he very aptly added the last words: neither circumcision counts for anything nor uncircumcision, and he spoke instead of a new creation. Of this he says elsewhere: “If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation” (2 Corinthians 5:17). If you are a new creation, he says, do not put yourself under the law. Whoever lives by the law lives in the world, but whoever lives in Christ has his citizenship in heaven. So “the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.”

lemmas.gloss: Hagarenes, descendants of Hagar and Ishmael
correspond to, stand in the same row with (Galatians 4:25)
citizenship, way of life as a citizen
live in plenty, feast, enjoy oneself (not 'luxury' in a moral sense here: the law's feasts)

choices.english: the law told them to enjoy plenty
choices.why: Severian means the law's commanded feasting and eating (he goes on: 'why were feasting and eating allowed?'). 'Commanded luxury' read as a moral contradiction; τρυφάω is 'live in plenty, feast'.

choices.term: Ζητεῖται διὰ τί νόμου ἀποσπῶν μέμνηται τῆς ἁμαρτίας
choices.english: People ask why, while he is drawing them away from the law, he speaks about sin.
choices.why: ἀποσπῶν governs νόμου: Paul is drawing the Galatians off the law. Old English 'one who pulls away through the law remembers sin' lost the agent.
rejected: he asks why one who pulls away through the law remembers sin

choices.why: The note answers why Paul turns to flesh and desire while drawing them from the law (5:16–18); the edition label 5:17 is kept.

choices.english: many were spending their money unwisely. They supplied the men who were urging them to keep the law and gave nothing to those who preached Paul's teaching.
choices.why: μέν/δέ contrast between supporting law-teachers and neglecting Paul's preachers (6:6–8); old English said 'consuming things unseasonably, providing nothing to those who keep the law', which reversed it.
rejected: many were consuming things unseasonably, providing nothing to those who keep the law (old)

choices.english: is sowing to the flesh and nothing more
choices.why: μόνον qualifies the sowing; old English 'sows into the flesh, sows only' was garbled.

choices.english: to be championing uncircumcision against circumcision
choices.why: ἀντιποιέομαι + genitive = lay claim to; old English 'making a substitute for circumcision' misread it.

choices.term: τὸ μὴ κατὰ σάρκα περιπατεῖν, ὡς λέγει ὁ Παῦλος
choices.english: not walking according to the flesh, as Paul puts it (Romans 8:4)
choices.why: Romans 8:4 has the phrase 'who walk not after the flesh'; the note has just cited Romans 8:8.

bible_refs.note: οἱ ἐν σαρκὶ ὄντες θεῷ ἀρέσαι οὐ δύνανται; Severian quotes it with κατὰ σάρκα ζῶντες
εἴ τις ἐν Χριστῷ, καινὴ κτίσις
4:24 'bearing children for slavery' echoed in the 4:25 note; 6:14 quoted at the end
